20+ Great Family Favorite Christmas Books for Kids (and a GIVEAWAY!)

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:28
Instaread

*** Hey! There’s a huge Christmas giveaway at the end of this post for over $700 in gift cards! Scroll down to learn more and enter. ***

Christmas is coming! Now is the time to buy or check out books for the season. We always try to build up our holiday library bit by bit each year. You can also start the wonderful tradition of wrapping the books up and opening one a day during the month of December!

If you’re looking for some picture books and chapter books that are fantastic read-alouds, this is for you! These are perfect for casual reading together, or you can bundle up some picture books for a Christmas Book Countdown!

For those of you with older kids in the mix these days, like me, I’ve added a section at the bottom with some of our favorite books your teens may enjoy.

Family Favorite Christmas Books for Kids

Here are 20+ great Christmas books for kids – some that are our favorites and some from our wish list! 

The Best Christmas Pageant Ever by Barbara Robinson – Such a fun and moving story!

Jotham’s Journey by Arnold Ytreeide – This is a great story that you read a chapter of each day leading up to Christmas. I would recommend doing it as a read aloud and editing on the fly if you have any sensitive kiddos. There are some scary and intense parts!

While we haven’t yet read these by Arnold Ytreeide, they are on the same track: 

  • Bartholomew’s Passage
  • Tabitha’s Travels
  • Ishtar’s Odyssey 

Familyman’s Christmas Treasury by Todd Wilson – Technically this is an audiobook but the stories included are SO fun and Christ-centered. We listen to them every year!

Christmas Miracle of Jonathan Toomey by Susan Wojciechowski – Such a beautiful story with lovely illustrations

An Orange for Frankie by Patricia Polacco – Lessons about giving!

Story of Holly and Ivy by Rumer Godden – This is such a cute story. It’s longer than we expected so we had to break it up into a few sessions but it was worth it!

Mary Engelbreit’s Nutcracker

 – Beautiful pictures and a delightful way to introduce this story to little ones.

The Very First Christmas Story by Paul Maier – An interesting way to tell the Christmas story that provides some historical tidbits and background as well. 


Drummer Boy
 – It’s a sweet, quiet story about a toy drummer boy that ends up at the feet of baby Jesus.


The Little Drummer Boy
 – We have the board book and the kids like to read/sing it all year long.


This Is the Stable
 – The kids love the repetition and we all love the story.


We Believe in Christmas
 – Made me cry. I can’t help it! Christmas stories that are actually about Jesus make me cry!


Tiny Baby Jesus
 – Very sweet. Goes back and forth between scenes of Jesus’ life as an adult and a baby.


Under the Star
 – Great repetition and counting.


The Crippled Lamb
 – Always a favorite. A lovely story about a lamb that is not like the rest but has a special purpose in God’s plan.


The Tale of the Three Trees: A Traditional Folktale
 – A fantastic book for Christmas and Easter!

On Our Wish List

Christmas Oranges by Linda Bethers


Legend of the Christmas Tree, The


Happy Birthday, Jesus!


Humphrey’s First Christmas


God Gave Us Christmas


Room for a Little One


The Shepherd’s Christmas Story


Song of the Stars: A Christmas Story


The Story of Christmas


Who is Coming to Our House?

More Christmas Books to Consider, Especially for Older Kids

American Christmas Stories, Volume 1 – These days I have older kids and so we’re using this as a Christmas/history connection for the month of December.

A Christmas Carol – This is a great one to dig into with your older kids as a book study this time of year. Most younger kids are familiar with the story, but there’s rich conversation to be had about the biblical themes of the book AND where it falls short (is it sharing the gospel or a works-based worldview?). It’s also a good one for discussing a biblical worldview of ghosts.

The Case for Christmas: A Journalist Investigates the Identity of the Child in the Manger – We have enjoyed several of Lee Strobel’s books. This would be an interesting one for older kids to add to their reading list!

The Story of the Other Wise Man by Henry van Dyke – An imaginative fictional older book that tells of a fourth wise man who misses meeting up with the other three and goes on a journey seeking the Messiah and learning about serving Him by serving others.

Little Women – We’ve pulled this one out a few times during the Christmas season over the years. It’s such a wonderful book and lovely for the holiday season!

What are your favorite Christmas books for kids?
